question: to the Commission Catherine Griset (PfE) Subject:

Under pressure and following a strike against his arrival at France Inter, journalist Charles Sapin eventually decided not to join this public media outlet. The act of censoring a journalist like this, whether for his actual or perceived political views, further tarnishes the image of the public audiovisual sector, which is increasingly and openly being monopolised by the left. Among the trade unions behind this act of censorship is the National Union of Journalists (SNJ)1. And yet, the Commission is consulting this extremist trade union, skilfully presented as a member of ‘civil society’, on topics such as freedom of the press2. 1.
Does the Commission publish a precise account of the requests and contributions made by this trade union or the European network to which it belongs3?
Does it intend to maintain relations with this far-left organisation, which is openly opposed to media pluralism and freedom of expression?
